newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Lines attack Australian quarantine fee rises.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Lines attack Australian quarantine fee rises.

text.p: Higher Australian Quarantine and Inspection Service (AQIS) charges would cost shipowners more than A$4 million extra a year and would have to be passed on to importers, Liner Shipping Services Ltd (LSS) said.
Representations would be made to AQIS and ministers of the Australian government, it said in a statement.
Additional charges would be passed on directly to importers unless a satisfactory resolution could be reached in the near future through a return to pre-September 1 charges, it said.
AQIS charges had increased from September 1 by between 100 percent and 300 percent for electronic clearance of containers.
This was not acceptable, Lew Russell, chief executive officer of LSS said.

"At a time when shipowners are making every effort to reduce costs and where there are constant complaints that Australian port charges are internationally uncompetitive, it is hard to believe that the government is increasing such costs without any increase in service," Russell said.

AQIS charges were increased to A$6 from A$3 per 20 foot container and to A$12 from A$3 per 40 foot container, with 40 foot containers comprising more than a third of containers discharged in Australia by LSS member lines, he said.
This item alone would cost shipowners more than A$4 million extra a year, he said.

Australia's Minister for Primary Industries and Energy John Anderson said the increased charges arose from a range of AQIS operational activities previously funded by the government as community service obligations being recovered from industry.
LSS is an organisation with 22 shipping line members.
